candidates.name: Chemchemal-Bazian Gas Pipeline
aka: Chemchemal field dedicated industrial gas pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Pearl Petroleum (Dana Gas / Crescent Petroleum, with OMV, MOL, RWE)
candidates.to: Bazian industrial area (cement and steel plants), Sulaymaniyah Governorate

evidence.note: Long-term gas sales agreements signed for up to 142 MMscf/d to cement and steel producers; 'a dedicated 40-km pipeline to the Bazian area' to be privately funded; deliveries begin H2 2027 with Chemchemal field startup.
Independent report of the same KRG-sanctioned offtake deals: Chemchemal gas to flow in 2027 under new supply agreements, with new dedicated pipeline infrastructure to Bazian.
Operator's own site confirms the Chemchemal development program under the KRG-granted concession (drilling, well testing, infrastructure construction; ~$160m program).

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster entry originates at Chemchemal. The existing Khormor-Pirdawood PP line (P6823, 180 km / 24 in) is the Khor Mor trunk feeding Erbil/Chemchemal/Bazian power stations; this is a NEW, separately funded 40 km line from the Chemchemal field itself to Bazian industrial consumers (142 MMscf/d, H2 2027). Distinct from P4047 (Khormor-Erbil, 36 in, construction) and P4053 (Erbil-Duhok).

candidates.name: Al-Faw Grand Port LNG-Abu Ghraib Supply Pipeline
aka: Abu Ghraib IPP gas supply pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Emirate Technology Company (BOO developer); Iraqi Council of Ministers approval
candidates.from: LNG reception infrastructure (jetty + FSRU), Al-Faw Grand Port, Basra Governorate
candidates.to: national gas network toward Abu Ghraib 3,000 MW combined-cycle plant (near Baghdad)

evidence.note: Cabinet approvals of 26 August (per PM's media office): Al-Faw Grand Port LNG reception infrastructure includes 'a jetty, a floating storage and regasification unit, and connecting pipelines - 17 kilometres at Al-Faw and 130km at Abu Ghraib'; each plant allocated ~400 MMscf/d of imported LNG; 25-year BOO with GE Vernova technology.
Corroborates the cabinet-approved package: Abu Ghraib 3,000 MW CCGT supplied with 'imported LNG via 130 km pipeline from Al-Faw port'; Al-Faw 3,000 MW plant supplied via 17 km pipeline from the FSRU.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster line runs from Al-Faw Grand Port northward into the network. Not P7435 (Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al-Basrah 42in/40km, the Khor Al-Zubair FSRU tie-in, completed 2025) and not P7434 (Mahmudiyah-Besmaya). Possible corridor overlap with shelved P5857 Zubair-Faw (105 km, 18 in) but that is a smaller domestic line in the opposite delivery direction; the 130 km figure and Abu Ghraib designation also do not fit P5857's spec. Caveat for consolidator: 130 km cannot physically reach Abu Ghraib (near Baghdad) from Al-Faw, so it is most likely the port-to-national-grid trunk segment, with onward delivery via the existing network; the associated 17 km Al-Faw FSRU-to-plant line is bundled here rather than emitted as a separate (feeder-scale) candidate.
